limits: Runs candidate wrapper bytes from an owned CPP layout, copying the current real lib.cicd.bootstrap and package initializers unchanged. JSON is valid YAML, decoded by real PyYAML, never a fake parser or checker. Only owned exit-0/exit-1 commands run. The wrapper owns the target; invocation cwd is a separate owned directory. A module import failure or an interpreter without PyYAML is unavailable, not unmet or clean. The control invocation requires real uv and uses uv run --isolated --frozen --no-dev to supply CPP runtime dependencies from uv.lock in a disposable environment, without syncing the project .venv. A cold uv cache needs network to obtain the locked packages and possibly a compatible Python; a populated cache can run offline. The wrapper itself still uses ambient python3: only the control subprocess gets the isolated interpreter on PATH. Missing PyYAML remains a real -S case. The pinned CI image has not been executed locally. The blind anchor routes check to list and therefore returns success without executing the blocker. Caller-shadow pairs add a regular lib package or raising yaml module outside CPP after the real PyYAML readiness check; the wrapper must still report the owned prerequisite verdict. The caller-PYTHONPATH pair supplies a regular lib.cicd.bootstrap that accepts every check; the real wrapper must ignore that search path and still evaluate its own blocker.

anchors.why: Keeps the corrected import root and CPP Python cwd but substitutes bootstrap list for bootstrap check. Every blocking case returns success because its command is never examined, including caller-shadow cases, while import failures remain unexaminable. This is the blind alternative to a working deploy prerequisite verdict, not a historical source claim.
